summary: The neutral stance held up on 10-27. The PM's decisions record adopting it, and nothing in close.json contradicts it. SPY value in the performance block rose from 599.13 to 602.49 (about +0.56%) on the day, so there was no risk-off break. The regime stayed on (SPY 765.37 vs 200-day 724.40, +5.66% in the 10-26 packet). The account day P/L was -$2.65, equity $600.52, drawdown 0.66%. The tech and communication weakness in the packet (QQQ 21d -4.34%, XLC 5d -5.67%) was the reason to stay at neutral rather than risk-on. The Industrials avoid call is supported: the held industrial-distribution name FAST fell 1.75% on the day while SPY rose. Limits of this review: I used only close.json, the packet and learning.json, and took my stance and tilts as quoted in the PM's reasoning rather than re-reading my own output file. One day of data is too little to grade confidence.

Keep describing bond strength as a short-term rally inside a downtrend, not a trend change. Gold is the weakest sleeve (GLD -6.5% 21d, -11.15% from its 200-day) and should stay in the avoid column. BTC is still a risky sleeve (21d -6.7%, 44% vol) even though it rose about 0.9% today.
